title: TH17 cells contribute to uveitis and scleritis and are inhibited by IL-27/STAT1 in the retina. \(6) Retinal cell isolation
protocol: Bleed mice by inserting a 24G needle below the rib cage in the center, directed slightly to the left and downwards at an angle of about 15-20°.
Enucleate eyes and place them in complete medium in a Petri dish for immediate retinal isolation.
Cut along the limbus of the eye and carefully remove the lens and cornea under a dissecting microscope.
Peel the retina off carefully and cut off the attachment at the optic nerve.
Mince retina tissue in collagenase/DNase digestion buffer containing complete medium with collagenase (1 mg/ml) + DNase (10 μg/ml).
Incubate retina in DNAse buffer at 37°C for 3 hours.
Pipette cells intermittently every 30 or 60 minutes using a 10 ml pipette.
After 3 hours, quench the digestion reaction with 5-10 fold volume of 10% FBS in medium.
Fill the tube with medium and centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 10 minutes.
Wash the pellet in complete medium twice.
Count the retinal cells.
Isolate naive syngeneic CD4+ T-helper cells (>95%).
Culture the naïve T cells in medium containing anti-CD3/anti-CD28 Abs under TH17 polarizing conditions (TGF-β1, IL-6, anti-IFNγ, and anti-IL-4 Abs) for 48 hours.
Add differentiating TH17 cells to freshly isolated retina cells at a ratio of 1 TH17 cell: 5 retina cells.
Propagate co-culture for additional 48 hours under the TH17 polarizing condition in the presence or absence of 10 μg/ml anti-IL-27p28 Abs.
Include controls with retinal cells alone.
Include controls with differentiating TH17 cells alone.
Add PMA and Ionomycin to the cultures for the last 5 hours.
Add Golgistop to the cultures for the last 1 hour.
Perform four-color cell surface/intracellular staining using antibodies against CD4, IL-17, IFN-γ, and CD44.
Use isotype control antibodies.
